He committed adultery with Bathsheba and arranged Uriah's death, then was confronted by Nathan (2 Samuel 11–12).
links.card_of: David: Shepherd from Bethlehem who became Israel's greatest king, a psalmist, and ancestor of the Messiah.

sentences: At David's order, he placed Uriah where he would be killed in battle (2 Samuel 11).
links.card_of: Joab: Son of David's sister Zeruiah and the commander of David's army.

sentences: He had the prophet Uriah brought back from Egypt and killed (Jeremiah 26).
links.card_of: Jehoiakim: A son of Josiah whom Pharaoh Neco made king of Judah, and who opposed Jeremiah.

sentences: The wife of Uriah whom David took in adultery; she later married David and became Solomon's mother.
David saw her bathing, slept with her, and arranged Uriah's death in battle (2 Samuel 11).
links.card_of: Bathsheba: The wife of Uriah whom David took in adultery; she later married David and became Solomon's mother.

sentences: A priest, son of Uriah, who served in Jerusalem in the days of Ezra and Nehemiah.
links.card_of: Meremoth: A priest, son of Uriah, who served in Jerusalem in the days of Ezra and Nehemiah.

sentences: Uriah built an altar copied from the model King Ahaz sent from Damascus (2 Kings 16).
Isaiah took Uriah the priest as a reliable witness to his written prophecy (Isaiah 8).
links.card_of: Uriah: A priest in Jerusalem under King Ahaz who built an altar from a pattern sent from Damascus.

sentences: Next to them, Meremoth son of Uriah repaired the following section of the wall (Nehemiah 3).
links.card_of: Hassenaah: Ancestor of a family whose members rebuilt Jerusalem's Fish Gate under Nehemiah.

sentences: The prophet Uriah of Kiriath-jearim was executed by King Jehoiakim (Jeremiah 26).
links.card_of: Kiriath-jearim: A Gibeonite town west of Jerusalem where the ark of the covenant stayed for twenty years.

sentences: While Joab besieged Rabbah, David sinned with Bathsheba and had Uriah killed (2 Samuel 11).
links.card_of: Rabbah: The capital city of the Ammonites, east of the Jordan.

sentences: Joab expected David to recall Abimelech's death at Thebez when hearing of Uriah's death (2 Samuel 11).
links.card_of: Thebez: A town near Shechem where Abimelech was mortally wounded by a millstone a woman dropped.

options.name: Uzziel
options.who: A Levite, son of Kohath and uncle of Moses and Aaron, whose descendants served at the tabernacle.

options.name: Uzziel
options.who: A Levite of Jeduthun's family who helped cleanse the temple under King Hezekiah.

sentences: A Levite, son of Uzziel, and chief of the Kohathite clans.
He is listed among the sons of Uzziel (Exodus 6).
links.card_of: Elizaphan: A Levite, son of Uzziel, and chief of the Kohathite clans.

sentences: A Levite of the clan of Kohath, son of Uzziel and cousin of Moses and Aaron.
Mishael is listed as a son of Uzziel, son of Kohath, with Elzaphan and Sithri (Exodus 6).
links.card_of: Mishael: A Levite of the clan of Kohath, son of Uzziel and cousin of Moses and Aaron.

options.name: Zedekiah
options.who: Son of Josiah and the last king of Judah before Babylon destroyed Jerusalem.

options.name: Zedekiah
options.who: A false prophet, son of Chenaanah, who urged Ahab to battle and struck the prophet Micaiah.

options.name: Zedekiah
options.who: A false prophet among the exiles in Babylon, son of Maaseiah, condemned by Jeremiah.

sentences: Zedekiah is made king, does evil, and rebels.
Zedekiah is captured, his sons are killed, and he is blinded.
Zedekiah rebels and refuses Jeremiah's word, while leaders and people defile the temple.
When King Zedekiah asks for help against Babylon, Jeremiah announces that God himself will fight against Jerusalem.
Zedekiah sends Pashhur son of Malchiah to inquire of the LORD.
Pestilence and sword will strike the city, and Zedekiah will be handed to Nebuchadnezzar.
Two baskets of figs show that exiles in Babylon will be restored while Zedekiah and those remaining will be ruined.
Zedekiah is urged to submit and live.
The false prophets Ahab and Zedekiah among the exiles are condemned.
Zedekiah confines Jeremiah for prophesying the city's fall.
Jeremiah warns Zedekiah of capture, and Judah is condemned for freeing and then re-enslaving their Hebrew servants.
Zedekiah will face Nebuchadnezzar but die in peace.
Jeremiah warns Zedekiah that Babylon will return, is arrested as a deserter, and is held in the court of the guard.
Zedekiah secretly asks for a word, and Jeremiah says he will be handed over.
Officials throw Jeremiah into a muddy cistern, Ebed-melech rescues him, and Jeremiah urges Zedekiah to surrender.
Jeremiah says surrender will spare Zedekiah and the city.
Zedekiah fears the Judeans and keeps the conversation secret.
Babylon captures Jerusalem, Zedekiah is blinded and exiled, and Jeremiah and Ebed-melech are spared.
Zedekiah flees but is caught near Jericho, and his sons are killed before him.
Zedekiah's rebellion leads to siege and famine.
A riddle of two eagles and a vine depicts Zedekiah's broken treaty with Babylon, followed by a promised cedar sprig.
Zedekiah broke his oath and will die in Babylon.
Zedekiah struck him, and Ahab had him imprisoned on bread and water (1 Kings 22).
links.card_of: Micaiah: Prophet of the LORD, son of Imlah, who foretold King Ahab's defeat and death in battle.

sentences: The king of Egypt in Zedekiah's day, named Hophra by Jeremiah, whose downfall Jeremiah and Ezekiel announced.
Ezekiel condemned Zedekiah for breaking his oath and seeking help from Egypt (Ezekiel 17).
links.card_of: Pharaoh Hophra: The king of Egypt in Zedekiah's day, named Hophra by Jeremiah, whose downfall Jeremiah and Ezekiel announced.

sentences: An Ethiopian eunuch in King Zedekiah's palace who rescued Jeremiah from a muddy cistern.
He appealed to King Zedekiah on behalf of Jeremiah, left to die in a cistern (Jeremiah 38).
links.card_of: Ebed-melech: An Ethiopian eunuch in King Zedekiah's palace who rescued Jeremiah from a muddy cistern.

sentences: A priest, son of Maaseiah, in Jerusalem during King Zedekiah's reign.
Zedekiah sent him to Jeremiah to inquire of the Lord about Nebuchadnezzar (Jeremiah 21).
Zedekiah again sent him to ask Jeremiah to pray for the people (Jeremiah 37).
links.card_of: Zephaniah: A priest, son of Maaseiah, in Jerusalem during King Zedekiah's reign.

sentences: Zedekiah made iron horns and prophesied that Ahab would push back the Syrians (1 Kings 22).
Micaiah said Zedekiah would see the truth when he hid in an inner chamber (1 Kings 22).
links.card_of: Zedekiah: A false prophet, son of Chenaanah, who urged Ahab to battle and struck the prophet Micaiah.

sentences: Jeremiah declared that Ahab and Zedekiah were prophesying lies to the exiles in the LORD's name (Jeremiah 29).
links.card_of: Ahab: A false prophet among the exiles in Babylon, son of Kolaiah, whom Jeremiah condemned for prophesying lies.

sentences: The father of Zedekiah, a false prophet in King Ahab's court.
His son Zedekiah made iron horns and promised Ahab victory over Syria (1 Kings 22).
Zedekiah son of Chenaanah struck the prophet Micaiah on the cheek (2 Chronicles 18).
links.card_of: Chenaanah: The father of Zedekiah, a false prophet in King Ahab's court.

sentences: A man of Libnah, grandfather of Kings Jehoahaz and Zedekiah through his daughter Hamutal; not the prophet.
Hamutal was also the mother of Zedekiah, Judah's last king (2 Kings 24).
The book of Jeremiah repeats that Zedekiah's mother was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah (Jeremiah 52).
links.card_of: Jeremiah: A man of Libnah, grandfather of Kings Jehoahaz and Zedekiah through his daughter Hamutal; not the prophet.

sentences: Father of Zephaniah, a leading priest in Jerusalem during King Zedekiah's reign.
His son Zephaniah was sent by Zedekiah to ask Jeremiah to inquire of the LORD (Jeremiah 21).
His son again carried Zedekiah's request for Jeremiah to pray for the people (Jeremiah 37).
links.card_of: Maaseiah: Father of Zephaniah, a leading priest in Jerusalem during King Zedekiah's reign.

sentences: Father of Zedekiah, a false prophet among the exiles in Babylon.
His son Zedekiah prophesied lies in the LORD's name among the exiles (Jeremiah 29).
Jeremiah foretold that the king of Babylon would roast Zedekiah and Ahab in the fire (Jeremiah 29).
links.card_of: Maaseiah: Father of Zedekiah, a false prophet among the exiles in Babylon.

sentences: Seraiah son of Neriah was quartermaster when he went with King Zedekiah to Babylon (Jeremiah 51).
links.card_of: Seraiah: A royal staff officer, brother of Baruch, who carried Jeremiah's prophecy against Babylon to that city.

sentences: The LORD said Zedekiah and Ahab son of Kolaiah were prophesying lies in his name (Jeremiah 29).
links.card_of: Zedekiah: A false prophet among the exiles in Babylon, son of Maaseiah, condemned by Jeremiah.

sentences: Daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah, wife of King Josiah, and mother of Kings Jehoahaz and Zedekiah.
She was also the mother of Zedekiah, Judah's last king (2 Kings 24).
Jeremiah's book repeats her name in recounting Zedekiah's reign and Jerusalem's fall (Jeremiah 52).
links.card_of: Hamutal: Daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah, wife of King Josiah, and mother of Kings Jehoahaz and Zedekiah.

sentences: He foretold that Nebuchadnezzar would kill Ahab and Zedekiah before the exiles' eyes (Jeremiah 29).
links.card_of: Kolaiah: The father of Ahab, a false prophet among the exiles in Babylon whom Jeremiah condemned.

sentences: Zedekiah's sons were killed before him at Riblah in the land of Hamath (2 Kings 25).
links.card_of: Hamath: A city-kingdom on the Orontes River in Syria, marking Israel's ideal northern border.

sentences: King Zedekiah fled toward the Arabah when Jerusalem fell (Jeremiah 52).
links.card_of: Arabah: The deep rift valley running from the Sea of Galilee through the Dead Sea to the Gulf of Aqaba.

sentences: At Riblah, Nebuchadnezzar killed Zedekiah's sons before his eyes and blinded him (2 Kings 25).
links.card_of: Riblah: A town in Syria used as a military headquarters by Egyptian and Babylonian kings.

sentences: Ebed-melech appeals for Jeremiah while King Zedekiah sits in the Benjamin Gate (Jeremiah 38).
links.card_of: Benjamin Gate: A gate on the north side of Jerusalem facing the territory of Benjamin.
